title: PRISM-MPF estimates Arctic sea-ice melt ponds from microwave observations
summary: PRISM-MPF used satellite microwave data to estimate pan-Arctic melt-pond fractions across eight melt seasons. Against an optical reference product, the model achieved a pooled R² of 0.532 and RMSE of 0.077, with weaker performance at high pond fractions.
organization: NOVA University Lisbon; University of Cambridge; ViaEO Consulting; University of Naples Federico II; CoNISMa

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.

evidence.tested: Leave-one-season-out evaluation over eight seasons and about 1.07 million co-located pixels, compared with an optical melt-pond fraction product.
evidence.unknown: Independent field validation was not established. Higher melt-pond fractions were harder to estimate, and the evaluation inherits limits of the optical reference.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost fused active and passive microwave observations with thermal and spatiotemporal variables to estimate melt-pond fraction.
